newsitem.title: USA: Governors call for victims' rights amendment.
newsitem.headline: Governors call for victims' rights amendment.

text.p: The nation's governors Tuesday called on Congress to pass an amendment to the Constitution to protect the rights of crime victims.

The National Governors Association, numbering 32 Republicans and 18 Democrats, said the amendment should guarantee crime victims the right to be fully informed on criminal proceedings and the release or escape of an offender.

Victims would also have the right to appear at criminal proceedings, to make statements before a sentence is imposed, to receive full restitution from an offender and to receive protection from threats of harm.

"The U.S. Constitution should not be changed for light and transient reasons but despite the existing protections in the states, victims of crimes seeking justice are often ignored by the criminal justice system," the resolution said.

"To require equal consideration for the rights of victims and offenders, the nation's governors urge the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives to pass a constitutional amendment guaranteeing victims' rights."
A constitutional amendment must be passed by two thirds majorities in both houses of Congress and be ratified by the legislatures of 38 of the 50 states. It does not require a presidential signature.
President Clinton and defeated Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole both supported a victims' rights amendment during last year's presidential campaign.
